text.en:
In the park Kiran counted twenty kinds of living things: a neem tree, a rose bush, grass, ants, a crow, a squirrel and a dog.
"How can I sort them?" he asked.
His teacher said, "Look at how they look and live. Group the ones that are alike."

There are millions of kinds of living things. We group them by similar features to understand them better. This is called classification.
Plants are grouped by size and stem. Herbs are small with a soft green stem. Shrubs are medium with several hard stems from the base. Trees are tall with one thick, hard trunk. Climbers and creepers need support or spread on the ground.
Animals are grouped too. Some have a backbone (fish, birds, reptiles, mammals) and some do not (insects, worms, snails).
Living things also live in different habitats: land, water, air, forests, deserts and mountains. Their body features help them live there. This is called adaptation.
Living things can be told apart from non-living things because they grow, need food and air, respond to their surroundings and reproduce.
We group living things that are alike. This is classification.
Herbs are small, shrubs have many hard stems, and trees have one thick trunk.
Animals can have a backbone or not. A fish and a bird have one. An ant does not.
A habitat is where a living thing lives. Its body suits that place, for example a fish has fins for water.

problem.en: A plant is tall and has one thick, hard trunk. Is it a herb, a shrub or a tree?

text.en: Look at the stem: it is a thick, hard trunk.

why.en: The stem type tells the group.

text.en: Herbs have soft stems and shrubs have many stems.

why.en: This plant has only one trunk.
A tall plant with a single trunk is a tree.

prompt.en: A friend says a rose bush and a mango tree are the same kind of plant. How will you explain the difference?

requiredIdeas.en: A rose bush is a shrub with many hard stems from the base.
A mango tree has one thick trunk and is much taller.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all plants with leaves are the same group.

points.en: We group living things by similar features.
Plants: herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers.
Habitat is where an organism lives and adaptation helps it live there.
